Karthik,

Quick update from our side — procurement flagged a mandatory vendor review next week which pushes sign-off on the MAP (and the SOW attachments) by roughly 10–14 business days. We still want to move forward but the team recommended a phased accept/PO approach rather than one big sign-off.

Key constraints:
- Vendor security intake: needs a call with our InfoSec (they asked for SOC2 evidence + answers to 6 additional controls).
- Budget committee meets only on 7/26 this month.

Thanks for the heads up, Tim — appreciate the visibility.

High level proposal from our side (to keep the evaluation moving):
1) Split the MAP into two buckets: Eval + Integration (Phase A) and Full Prod enablement (Phase B). We can accept a Phase A PO that covers the evaluation window and support hours.
2) Fast-track the SOC2 evidence and a short InfoSec sync (30m). Connor can join and walk through our evidence pack and isolation controls.
3) Offer a 2-week extension on the evaluation credits (no cost) if procurement needs more time; ties you to a Phase A PO commitment when ready.

I'll loop in Laura for billing/contract mechanics and Neha for procurement/legal exceptions if needed. Connor — can you confirm availability for the SOC2 InfoSec sync tomorrow afternoon?

Karthik

Subject: Re: MAP review — containment ladder & annotated root-cause timeline for Globex close

Thanks all — the InfoSec sync was helpful. A few quick outcomes and remaining risks so we keep a single source of truth for the close path: 

Annotated timeline (agreed):
- 7/13: InfoSec sync (done) — Connor walked through controls.
- 7/16: Globex procurement to circulate revised vendor questions.
- 7/26: Budget committee review (hard stop for PO approval).
- 8/09: Tentative production onboarding (if budget clears on 7/26).

Open risks (top 3):
1) Budget commit slips again (impact: >2 week delay to prod). Mitigation: Phase A PO to capture evaluation effort + pre-approved billing code so we can start immediately after budget sign-off.
2) Additional InfoSec asks (impact: blocks early production routing). Mitigation: Connor's pinned model + enhanced logging; we offered an InfoSec sandbox for their review.
3) Procurement legal redlines (impact: enlarge contract negotiation window). Mitigation: Laura/Neha to prepare a prioritized redline list and offer a targeted concession matrix to limit negotiation to 3 items.

Decision asks for Redwood:
- Can you confirm we will hold the 2-week evaluation-credit with the Phase A PO binding?
- If budget misses 7/26, what is the latest date Redwood can absorb the evaluation cost before we need to re-negotiate pricing?

Thanks again — keeping this documented in the MAP helps the execs see progress.

Tim
